method_note: Headlines are copied from page metadata (og:title / title) or the in-page headline as returned by a read-only page fetch on 2026-11-23. Where a page showed more than one headline variant (e.g. updated headline vs. original), the variant is stated in verification_notes. Dates are as shown in page metadata or the page body; 'date' on each entry is the date of first public disclosure/occurrence per sources.

entries.description: Optus experienced a nation-wide network outage on 8 November 2023 that caused significant disruption across Australia for individuals and businesses, and the ACMA later found 2,145 people were not given access to the emergency call service during the outage.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per the earliest verified mainstream piece (ABC, 8 Nov 2023): more than 10 million customers were affected by the Optus outage (headline claim).
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Cause not stated in the verified headline; the ACMA's later investigation report attributes it to self-isolation of core network routers. Triple Zero impact figures (2,145 people; 369 missed welfare checks) were only established in the ACMA investigation, published 8 Nov 2024.

ACMA headline/date verified by opening the page (dcterms.date + on-page '08 November 2024'). ACMA investigation report PDF and infrastructure.gov.au review page appeared in search results but were not opened.

entries.description: DP World Australia detected unauthorised access to its Australian corporate network on Friday 10 November 2023 and disconnected internet connectivity to contain it, which stopped normal operation of key systems at its ports in Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane and Fremantle.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per ABC (11 Nov 2023): operator began responding on Friday; ships could unload but freight could not leave the port site; internet connectivity was disconnected; Home Affairs minister and National Cyber Security Coordinator involved; operator responsible for 40 per cent of maritime freight.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Duration of disruption ('likely to continue for a number of days' per government statement quoted by ABC); nature/extent of the intrusion. DP World's 28 Nov 2023 statement is the verified later update.

entries.description: Medibank reported on 13 October 2022 that it detected unusual activity on its network and would isolate and remove access to some customer-facing systems; the OAIC later alleged a data breach of Medibank and ahm exposed the personal information of 9.7 million Australians.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per Reuters (13 Oct 2022): unusual activity detected; Medibank taking steps to contain the incident and removing access to some customer-facing systems; shares on trading halt; Medibank said there was no evidence at that stage that sensitive data including customer data had been accessed.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Whether customer data had been accessed or stolen (Medibank said no evidence at that stage); on 19 Oct 2022 Medibank said it had received messages from a group wishing to negotiate over alleged removal of customer data; the OAIC's 9.7 million figure and 25 Oct 2022 breach notification date appear only in the 2024 OAIC release.

entries.description: Latitude Financial said on 16 March 2023 it had been hit by a cyber-attack in which an attacker used employee login credentials to steal personal information held by two service providers; the company later said about 14 million customer records were stolen.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per Guardian/iTnews (16 Mar 2023): more than 100,000 identification documents and 225,000 customer records stolen; employee login credentials used; data held by two service providers; share trading suspended.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Total scale: on 27 Mar 2023 Latitude said about 14m customer records (7.9m driver licence numbers, 53,000 passport numbers, 6.1m other records) had been stolen, far above the initial figures.

entries.description: On 15 June 2022 AEMO suspended the wholesale electricity spot market in all National Electricity Market regions because a confluence of events made it impossible to continue operating the spot market while ensuring secure and reliable supply, and it lifted the suspension from 2pm on 24 June 2022.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per SMH (15 Jun 2022): AEMO made an unprecedented intervention to suspend trading across the east coast electricity network; NSW Energy Minister urged residents to minimise non-critical usage between 5.30pm and 8.30pm.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Duration (suspension later lifted 24 Jun 2022, per AEMO); whether blackouts would occur (SMH description: 'reduce the risk of electricity blackouts').

entries.description: Qantas said on 2 July 2025 that a cyber criminal targeted one of its airline contact centres and gained access to a third-party customer servicing platform containing customer data (initially reported as six million customer accounts).
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per Reuters (2 Jul 2025): hacker targeted a call centre and accessed a third-party customer service platform holding six million names, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates and frequent flyer numbers.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Final affected count (a later Qantas update/third-party sources cited 5.7 million; not verified from an opened page); whether data would be released (Qantas page update of 12 Oct 2025 says data was released by cyber criminals).

entries.description: The national cyber security coordinator announced a large-scale ransomware data breach on 16 May 2024, which the ABC confirmed was at e-script provider MediSecure; MediSecure later said about 12.9 million individuals may have had personal and health information exposed.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per ABC (16 May 2024): the ABC could confirm MediSecure was the organisation at the centre of the breach; MediSecure's website was pulled; MediSecure said a cyber security incident affected personal and health information; AFP also looking into the breach.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Number of people affected (12.9 million disclosed by MediSecure in July 2024); MediSecure spokesperson said it was too early to detail the nature and extent; ABC later reported the theft itself took place earlier and continued until November 2023.

entries.description: On 17 June 2021 an hour-long outage hit most major Australian lenders (including CBA, Westpac and ANZ) and other websites; Reuters reported it was caused by a glitch at content delivery network provider Akamai.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per Reuters (17 Jun 2021): websites of dozens of financial institutions and airlines in Australia and the US were briefly down on Thursday, attributed to server-related glitches at CDN provider Akamai; SMH: online banking resumed after an hour-long outage that also disrupted the RBA and Virgin Australia sites.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Root cause was initially unclear in the original SMH URL slug ('urgently investigating'); later reporting said an Akamai software bug, not a cyber-attack or vulnerability (Reuters search excerpt).

entries.description: On Monday 26 June 2023 Commonwealth Bank suffered an outage, starting around 7:30am AEST, that left customers unable to access accounts, including transfers and payments, for several hours before CBA said it was resolved.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per Guardian/AFR (26 Jun 2023): customers could not check balances or transfer funds in the Netbank app; some could not make purchases; CBA later said it had resolved the outage and advised some payments would be delayed.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Cause: Guardian description says CBA reported the issue resolved without reporting the cause.

entries.description: Optus announced on 22 September 2022 that a cyber attack had compromised customer information; the OAIC opened an investigation on 11 October 2022 into the data breach made public by Optus on 22 September 2022.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per ABC (22 Sep 2022): Optus said it had been hit by a cyber attack that compromised customer information (names, dates of birth, phone numbers, email addresses) and that the attack had been shut down.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Scale and data types: Reuters (23 Sep 2022) reported Optus would contact up to 10 million customers and that addresses, driver licence and passport numbers were accessed.

entries.description: During a network upgrade on 18 September 2025 a technical failure on the Optus network meant triple-0 calls could not go through, and three people were reported to have died; the ACMA later launched Federal Court proceedings alleging Optus breached two legal obligations on 1,005 occasions during the outage.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per ABC (19 Sep 2025): three people, including an eight-week-old baby, died after a technical failure on the Optus network meant triple-0 calls were unable to go through; Optus CEO said approximately 600 customers were potentially impacted during a network upgrade.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Full number of failed calls and affected states (the ABC piece says 'several states' and 'hundreds of triple-0 calls'); ACMA's 1,005-occasion allegation came later (minister statement dated 2026-07-30).

entries.description: On 18 November 2025 an IT/communications issue at Airservices Australia prevented flight plans being processed automatically, forcing manual processing and causing delays at Melbourne, Perth and Adelaide airports before flights resumed.
entries.confirmed_at_first_report: Per Nine (18 Nov 2025): large-scale IT outage prevented Airservices Australia from processing flight plans automatically; staff entered details manually; major delays in Melbourne, Perth and Adelaide. Per news.com.au: Airservices confirmed it was working to address an issue with systems at its Melbourne Air Traffic Service Centre.
entries.unconfirmed_at_first_report: Root cause: Australian Aviation (19 Nov 2025) says it understood the issue was unrelated to a global Cloudflare outage; no official cause statement was opened.
